questions.q: What is the key difference between an event handler and a logging provider?
options: An event handler runs a workflow in response to an event; a logging provider just records what happened, without taking any action
They are two names for the exact same feature in SSIS Designer
Logging providers can only be configured programmatically, never through the UI
Event handlers write to sysssislog; logging providers send e-mail
questions.explain: Event handlers actively respond to an event (e.g. sending an e-mail); logging simply writes a record of what happened for later review — most real packages use both together.

questions.q: Which log provider requires no connection manager at all?
options: SSIS log provider for Windows Event Log
SSIS log provider for Text files
SSIS log provider for SQL Server
SSIS log provider for XML files
questions.explain: The Windows Event Log provider writes directly into the Windows Application event log — SSIS creates that log automatically without needing a connection manager.

questions.q: In the Configure SSIS Logs dialog's Containers pane, what does a dimmed checkbox on a child container mean?
options: The container is inheriting its parent's logging configuration rather than defining its own
The container has logging permanently disabled and cannot be changed
The container failed the last time the package ran
The container is using a different provider type than its parent
questions.explain: By default, child containers inherit their parent's logging settings (shown dimmed); clicking the checkbox twice breaks that inheritance so the container can define its own.

questions.q: What does the Advanced view on the Details tab add over the Basic view?
options: It expands each loggable event to show individual information categories (Computer, Operator, SourceName, MessageText, etc.) you can select or clear
It lets you write custom SQL queries against the log table
It enables logging to multiple providers simultaneously, which Basic view does not allow
It shows a live, real-time stream of log entries as the package runs
questions.explain: Basic view only lists events to check; Advanced view breaks each selected event down into the specific information categories SSIS can record for it.

questions.q: Which log provider writes to the sysssislog table?
options: SSIS log provider for SQL Server
SSIS log provider for Text files
SSIS log provider for SQL Server Profiler
SSIS log provider for XML files
questions.explain: The SQL Server log provider writes run-time log entries into the sysssislog table in a SQL Server database, via an OLE DB connection manager.
